abraham-de-moivre.label: De Moivre's Formula
abraham-de-moivre.description: A fundamental bridge between complex numbers and trigonometry.

abraham-de-moivre.label:
Normal
            Approximation to Binomial
abraham-de-moivre.description: De Moivre was the first to discover the normal curve as an approximation to the binomial distribution.

adrien-marie-legendre.label: Legendre Polynomials
adrien-marie-legendre.description: Solutions to Legendre's differential equation, essential in physics and engineering.

adrien-marie-legendre.label: Legedre Symbol
adrien-marie-legendre.description: A notation in number theory to specify quadratic residues.

andrei-andreyevich-markov.label: Markov Property
andrei-andreyevich-markov.description: The principle that the future state depends only on the current state, not the past.
andrei-andreyevich-markov.equation: P(X_{n+1} = x \mid X_1 = x_1, \dots, X_n = x_n) = P(X_{n+1} = x \mid X_n = x_n)

andrei-andreyevich-markov.label: Markov Inequality
andrei-andreyevich-markov.description: A fundamental bound in probability theory.

andrey-nikolaevich-kolmogorov.label: Kolmogorov Axioms
andrey-nikolaevich-kolmogorov.description: The foundation of modern probability theory.

andrey-nikolaevich-kolmogorov.label: Chapman-Kolmogorov Equation
andrey-nikolaevich-kolmogorov.description: Relates joint probability distributions of stochastic processes.

augustus-de-morgan.label: De Morgan's Laws
augustus-de-morgan.description: Fundamental rules of logic and set theory relating conjunctions and disjunctions.

blaise-pascal.label: Pascal's Identity
blaise-pascal.description: The recurrence relation defining Pascal's Triangle.

blaise-pascal.label: Principle of Hydrostatics
blaise-pascal.description: Pascal's law regarding pressure in a fluid.

carl-gustav-jacob-jacobi.label:
Jacobian
            Determinant
carl-gustav-jacob-jacobi.description: Used for changing variables in multiple integrals.

carl-gustav-jacob-jacobi.label: Jacobi Identity
carl-gustav-jacob-jacobi.description: A property of the Poisson bracket and Lie algebras.

david-hilbert.label:
Einstein-Hilbert
            Action
david-hilbert.description: The action that yields the Einstein field equations of general relativity.

david-hilbert.label: Hilbert Space Inner Product
david-hilbert.description: Generalizing Euclidean space to infinite dimensions.

evangelista-torricelli.label: Torricelli's Law
evangelista-torricelli.description: Describes the speed of fluid flowing out of an opening.

evangelista-torricelli.label:
Torricelli's Trumpet (Gabriel's
            Horn)
evangelista-torricelli.description: A geometric figure with infinite surface area but finite volume.

evariste-galois.label: Galois Group Solvability
evariste-galois.description: The criterion for whether a polynomial is solvable by radicals.
evariste-galois.equation: \text{Gal}(L/K) \text{ is a solvable group} \iff \text{Solvable by radicals}

francois-viete.label: Vieta's Formulas
francois-viete.description: Relations between the coefficients of a polynomial and sums/products of its roots.

georg-friedrich-bernhard-riemann.label: Riemann Zeta Function
georg-friedrich-bernhard-riemann.description: The subject of the Riemann Hypothesis regarding the distribution of prime numbers.

george-boole.label: Boolean Algebra
george-boole.description: The algebraic structure that underlies modern digital logic.

godfrey-harold-hardy.label:
Hardy-Weinberg
            Principle
godfrey-harold-hardy.description: Allele frequencies in a population remain constant in equilibrium.

godfrey-harold-hardy.label: Hardy-Littlewood Circle Method
godfrey-harold-hardy.description: An analytic technique for estimating the number of solutions to additive number theory problems.

hermann-minkowski.label: Spacetime Interval
hermann-minkowski.description: The invariant metric of special relativity combining space and time.

isaac-newton.label:
Law of
            Universal Gravitation
isaac-newton.description: Newton introduced this in 1687, unifying celestial and terrestrial mechanics under a single mathematical law.

isaac-newton.label: Binomial Series
isaac-newton.description:
Developed in the 1660s, this expansion was part of Newton’s broader creation of infinite series methods before
        calculus was formalized.

isaac-newton.label: Newton–Leibniz Calculus (Fluxions)
isaac-newton.description:
Newton devised fluxions in the mid-1660s, though publication delays fueled the famous priority dispute with
        Leibniz.

jacob-jacques-bernoulli.label: Law of Large Numbers
jacob-jacques-bernoulli.description: Bernoulli proved the first version of this fundamental probability theorem.

jean-le-rond-d-alembert.label: Wave Equation
jean-le-rond-d-alembert.description: The first solution to the vibrating string problem.

johann-bernoulli.label: L'Hôpital's Rule
johann-bernoulli.description: Taught to L'Hôpital by Johann Bernoulli (for a fee).

johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.label:
Fundamental Theorem of
            Algebra
johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.description: Gauss gave the first rigorous proof in 1799, helping legitimize complex numbers within mainstream mathematics.
johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.equation: p(z) = 0 \quad \text{has at least one complex root}

johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.label: Gaussian Integral
johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.description:
This result appeared in Gauss’s early 19th-century work on probability and error theory tied to astronomical
        observations.

johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.label: Gauss’s Law (Electrostatics)
johann-carl-friedrich-gauss.description:
Developed in the 1830s, this law became foundational to electromagnetism decades before Maxwell unified the
        field.

johann-peter-gustav-lejeune-dirichlet.label: Dirichlet Series
johann-peter-gustav-lejeune-dirichlet.description: A generalization of the Zeta function.

johann-peter-gustav-lejeune-dirichlet.label: Class Number Formula
johann-peter-gustav-lejeune-dirichlet.description: Relating algebraic number theory quantities to L-function values.

john-von-neumann.label: Von Neumann Entropy
john-von-neumann.description: Extension of classical entropy to quantum mechanics.

john-wallis.label: Wallis Product
john-wallis.description: An infinite product for \(\pi\) involving only rational numbers.

joseph-fourier.label: Fourier Series
joseph-fourier.description:
Introduced in 1807, this idea was initially controversial for claiming arbitrary functions could be represented
        by trigonometric series.

joseph-fourier.label: Fourier Transform
joseph-fourier.description:
Developed from Fourier’s heat theory, this transform later became essential to physics, engineering, and signal
        processing.

joseph-fourier.label: Heat Equation
joseph-fourier.description:
Fourier formulated this equation in 1807 while studying heat diffusion, laying groundwork for modern partial
        differential equations.

joseph-louis-lagrange.label: Lagrange Multipliers
joseph-louis-lagrange.description: Method for finding local maxima/minima subject to constraints.

jules-henri-poincare.label:
Poincaré
            Recurrence Theorem
jules-henri-poincare.description: States that certain systems will eventually return to a state very close to the initial one.

jules-henri-poincare.label:
Poincaré-Hopf Index
            Theorem
jules-henri-poincare.description: Relating vector fields to the Euler characteristic.

leonardo-pisano-fibonacci.label: Fibonacci Sequence
leonardo-pisano-fibonacci.description: A sequence where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.

leonardo-pisano-fibonacci.label: Golden Ratio limit
leonardo-pisano-fibonacci.description: The ratio of consecutive Fibonacci numbers converges to \(\phi\).

leonhard-euler.label: Euler’s Identity
leonhard-euler.description:
Published in the 1740s, this formula became iconic for uniting analysis, geometry, and arithmetic at a time when
        complex numbers were still controversial.

leonhard-euler.label:
Euler’s Formula (Complex
            Exponentials)
leonhard-euler.description:
Euler introduced this in the mid-18th century, giving complex numbers a geometric interpretation that transformed
        trigonometry and analysis.

leonhard-euler.label: Basel Problem Solution
leonhard-euler.description: Euler solved this famous problem in 1734, astonishing contemporaries by linking infinite series to \(\pi\).

leonhard-euler.label:
Euler–Lagrange
            Equation (Euler’s Original Form)
leonhard-euler.description:
Euler developed this equation in the 1740s while founding the calculus of variations, later refined with
        Lagrange.

leonhard-euler.label:
Euler’s Totient
            Formula
leonhard-euler.description:
Introduced in the 1760s, this identity emerged from Euler’s systematic generalization of Fermat’s
        number-theoretic ideas.

leonhard-euler.label:
Euler’s Product
            Formula for the Zeta Function
leonhard-euler.description:
Euler discovered this in 1737, revealing for the first time a deep analytic link between prime numbers and
        infinite series.

leonhard-euler.label: Euler’s Identity for Homogeneous Functions
leonhard-euler.description:
Formulated in the 1750s, this result arose from Euler’s broader effort to formalize scaling laws in mechanics and
        geometry.
leonhard-euler.equation: x f_x + y f_y = k f

marie-sophie-germain.label: Sophie Germain Primes
marie-sophie-germain.description: A prime \(p\) where \(2p+1\) is also prime, crucial in her work on Fermat's Last Theorem.

pierre-de-fermat.label: Fermat's Principle
pierre-de-fermat.description: Light travels between two points along the path of least time.

pierre-simon-laplace.label: Laplace Transform
pierre-simon-laplace.description: Transforms differential equations into algebraic ones.

rene-descartes.label:
Descartes' Rule of
            Signs
rene-descartes.description: Determines the number of positive real roots of a polynomial.

rene-descartes.label: Polyhedral Formula
rene-descartes.description: A precursor to Euler's formula for polyhedra.

simeon-denis-poisson.label: Poisson Distribution
simeon-denis-poisson.description: Probability of a given number of events occurring in a fixed interval.

simeon-denis-poisson.label: Poisson Equation
simeon-denis-poisson.description: Generalization of Laplace's equation for systems with charge/mass density.

srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.label: Ramanujan’s Series for \(\frac{1}{\pi}\)
srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.description:
Discovered in 1914, this formula stunned mathematicians and later became central to high-precision computations
        of \(\pi\).

srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.label: Hardy–Ramanujan Partition Formula
srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.description:
Derived in 1918, this asymptotic formula revolutionized understanding of integer partitions using analytic
        methods.

srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.label: Ramanujan’s Continued Fractions
srinivasa-aiyangar-ramanujan.description:
These formulas emerged from Ramanujan’s notebooks and baffled mathematicians until modern modular theory
        explained them.

william-rowan-hamilton.label: Hamiltonian
william-rowan-hamilton.description: The operator corresponding to the total energy of the system.

william-rowan-hamilton.label: Quaternion Rules
william-rowan-hamilton.description: The fundamental formula for quaternion multiplication carved into Broome Bridge.
